description: When a child is hurt at a Georgia day care, violations of licensing standards and Bright From The Start regulations may support a negligence per se claim.
shortAnswer: When an injury to a child occurs at a day care center it is probable that State of Georgia licensing standards and Bright From The Start regulations have been violated. When that injury was caused by a failure to adhere to them, this violation of Georgia law or regulation may form the basis of a negligence per se claim.

faq.q: Who enforces safety rules for day care centers in Georgia?
faq.a: Bright From The Start (also known as the Georgia Department of Early Care and Learning) is the agency charged with enforcing Georgia's child safety, health and welfare laws in connection with child care learning centers.

faq.q: Do the same regulations apply to every Georgia day care?
faq.a: The applicability of different aspects of the regulations varies depending on whether a day care center is categorized as a "family day care home," "group day care home," "day care center" or some other designation. It is important to determine the legal designation of what kind of child care learning center your child was attending before researching which regulations apply.

faq.q: What are Georgia's infant sleep safety rules for family day care homes?
faq.a: Under Section 290-2-3-.19, in order to reduce the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), staff shall put an infant to sleep on the infant's back unless the home has been provided a physician's written statement authorizing another sleep position. Any crib used for sleeping shall have no pillows, quilts, comforters, bumper pads, sheepskins, stuffed toys, or other soft items.
